text:
maya: FYI prod token/sec dropped ~27% right after the canary merge (PR #4621). saw it at 17:02 UTC.
tonny: Any alerts?
maya: alert from perf-monitor: tokens/sec p95 dropped 26% across ctb-enabled pools. rollout bot shows canary to 80% at 17:01.
ci-bot: CI perf test failed: "ctb_throughput_smoke" — 12% regression on seq=16; build=2026-3301.
sophia: quick check of kernel-selection logs: lots of fallback to `memcopy` kernel for small batches. looks like kernel-affinity heuristic flipped to prefer memcpy path.
adrian: did PR #4621 touch coalesce/stride heuristics?
maya: yes — it changed coalesce window heuristic to use stride-based grouping when avg_seq > 32. merged without a perf flag.
liam: logs show coalesce window shrank 48->12 for many small sequence requests; batch size distribution shifted down. KV cache hit rate stable.
maya: profiler snippet (redwood-prof):
```
# profiler excerpt
seq=8 batch=3 kernel=memcpy_dev_to_dev time_ms=1.9
seq=8 batch=3 kernel=matmul_small time_ms=0.6
```
sophia: that matches: more memcpy ops in the hot path -> serial GPU memcpy ops and throughput collapse.
adrian: can we revert PR4621 on canary now? rollout is a blocker.
maya: opening rollback. will revert canary to previous commit in 5m unless objections.
tonny: +1 revert now, block rollout.
ci-bot: Rollback triggered: deploy/revert/3305556800 by maya.
maya: post-revert numbers: tokens/sec back to baseline within 2m. before merge: ~145k tok/s, after merge: ~106k tok/s, after revert: ~143k tok/s.
sophia: action items: add CI perf gate that runs CTB throughput smoke for seq=8/16/64 on merges that touch coalesce/kernel-selection code.
adrian: also add kernel-selection trace capture and a unit test asserting coalesce->stride mapping for small/medium seqs. feature-flag the new heuristic.
liam: note — KV cache didn't change, this is purely batching/coalesce -> smaller batches -> memcpy route. good to call out in perf writeup.
maya: filing follow-up issue and linking results. issue: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-2187
tonny: thanks everyone. moving this to rollout-hold :thumbsup:
